Qualcomm has revealed its quarterly results and forecast earnings for the current quarter that fell short of expectations. The CEO told Reuters that supply constraints will cause its revenue from Apple products to decline faster than expected. Details below.

Qualcomm is "replacing Apple" with its data center business

Over the past few years, Apple has been pushing forward with its plan to replace Qualcomm's modem chips with its own components, building on the foundation of its 2019 acquisition of Intel's smartphone modem business.

For its part, Qualcomm has repeatedly assured investors that it is prepared for the loss of Apple's business. CEO Cristiano Amon is now warning that the decline will accelerate, partly because ongoing supply constraints mean the company is receiving a smaller share of components than originally anticipated.

Speaking to Reuters, Amon said Qualcomm "expects revenue from Apple products to accelerate its decline starting in the fourth quarter, because supply constraints mean its share of components for the next-generation iPhone launch will be far lower than the previously estimated 20%."

He added that Qualcomm has been offsetting the impact of losing Apple's orders by expanding beyond smartphones, and expects its data center division to generate $5 billion in revenue in fiscal year 2027:

It is worth noting that Qualcomm's relationship with Apple extends beyond supplying modem components. The company also collects patent licensing fees from Apple, separately from chip sales, and even if Apple switches to its own modem technology, these licensing fees (for the time being) will continue to be collected.

In 2019, the two companies reached a settlement over their long-running legal disputes and signed a six-year licensing agreement. Apple subsequently exercised an option to extend the agreement by two years, meaning it will remain valid until March 2027.
